headline: Explained how to apply for Community Preservation Act grants, with pre-applications due October 8 and full applications due January 13.
summary: This was an annual informational session on the Community Preservation Act and grant applications. Speakers described eligible projects, the 10% set-aside, the 5% administrative limit, and about $2.5M available for FY27.

2. Welcome and History of Community Preservation Act 18 
• Massachusetts General Law / Beverly Local Ordinance 19 
 20 
Pearl gave a brief history of the Community Preservation Act, including when Beverly created 21 
its own local ordinance. 22 
 23 
• General Purpose of CPA / Local Community Preservation Plan 24 
 25 
Pearl explained that the intent behind CPA was to create a funding source that could be directed 26 
to projects that enhance people’s quality of life. The categories for project funding under the 27 
CPA include community housing, open space, and historic preservation. Recreational land is also 28 
a category but does not rise to the same level as the others in the statute. Activities within those 29 
are to acquire, create, preserve, support, rehabilitate, etc. The City has a Community Preservation 30 
Plan which outlies the goals, objectives, and criteria. The Plan is scheduled to be updated shortly.   31 
 32 
• Brief Overview of the Range of Projects Previously Funded 33 
 34 
Pearl stated that, over the past 14 years, $12M has been invested in the project categories. 100 35 
projects have been funded from 120 applications.  36 
 37 
• Examples of Successful Projects 38 
 39 
Marino reviewed examples of successful projects from over the years. In terms of recreation 40 
projects throughout the City, since the adoption of the CPA, it has funded $3.2M for 32 41 
recreation project. Of that, roughly $400,000 was for non-City Recreation Department projects, 42 
such as passive recreational areas in the City.   43 
 44 
• CPA Budget and Available Balances 45

Pearl explained that the CPA is set up to take advantage of a local surcharge on people’s 47 
property tax. It is a 1% charge on top of the property tax, not the property value, when is then 48 
matched with State funds. Every year the State match is variable. It is set by the Department of 49 
Revenue at the beginning of the program. The surcharge brings in most of the revenue from year 50 
to year. Every year the Committee votes to adopt a budget which identifies what the estimated 51 
revenues are and where the funds will be spent. The Community Preservation Act requires that 52 
10% of the budget each year much be spent in the three primary categories: historic resources, 53 
community housing, and open space. 5% can also be set aside for administrative costs. For 54 
FY27, the Committee will have balances carrying over in the specific categories, a balance 55 
carrying over in the general budget reserve, and a grand total of approximately $2.5M available 56 
for projects that applications are received for. $1.5M is available money that could be spent 57 
across the categories. The remaining balances in the three categories can only be spent in those 58 
categories.  59 
 60 
3. Discuss Needs, Possibilities, and Resources in Beverly 61 
 62 
There were suggestions made for potential projects that involve accessible boating, space for 63 
programs, bike lanes/trails, sustainability measures such as drought-tolerant plantings, dog 64 
specific areas, a co-housing space, etc. 65 
 66 
4. How to Apply for CPA Funds 67 
• CPA Rules per Statute 68 
• Project Eligibility 69 
• Grant Round Schedule 70 
• Application and Materials 71 
 72 
Pearl explained that the rules of the State statute apply locally, including the 10% set aside in the 73 
three categories, and the 5% limit for administrative costs. Recipients can be public or private 74 
entities, and they can be non-profit and for-profit organizations, and can include the City. This 75 
Committee has approved and awarded grants to all of those types of organizations in the past. 76 
Allowable uses include the action verbs that were previously mentioned: acquisition, creation, 77 
preservation, rehabilitation, restoration, and support. An applicant should consider how the 78 
action verbs are defined by the statute. Preserving something under CPA means that the project 79 
will prevent the loss of certain things. Support is not funded in any category except for housing. 80 
Open space projects can only deal with rehabilitation or restoration if the asset was acquired or 81 
created with CPA funding, and the same is true for the housing. The recreation category provides 82 
a lot of flexibility for improvements to playgrounds and parks but it cannot fund maintenance. 83 
 84 
Pearl explained that this evening’s meeting, on September 10th, is the annual informational 85 
meeting. At the beginning of each Committee meeting, there is time on the agenda for a Q&A 86 
which applicants should utilize. If an applicant is considering an historic preservation project, the 87 
property that is being proposed for the project has to be determined Significant by the Historic 88 
District Commission. This is done through filling out a form and submitting it for one of the 89 
HDC’s regularly scheduled meetings. There is a deadline of September 16th for consideration at 90

the HDC meeting on September 23rd. Pre-applications are due on October 8th. The Committee 91 
will then determine if they are eligible and invited to submit full applications. This information 92 
should be released by November 30th, with full applications due January 13th. After they are 93 
submitted, the Committee will post the full applications for public comment. That public 94 
comment period will end on February 1st. The Committee will then have regular meetings to 95 
deliberate on all of the applications. By April or May, the Committee will make a 96 
recommendation to City Council on which projects to fund. The City Council then has to vote up 97 
or down on those. Once the City Council approves, the Committee will announce the awards and 98 
enter into a grant agreement with the applicants in order to start the projects.  99
